data.result:
carbonate [evidence] Carbonate (CRISM, Mg-carbonate prototype), interim
Measures: Orbital spectral detection of the 'Mg-Carbonate' prototype class in the CRISM mineral map, as an ordinal evidence tier: strong_orbital (3) = bold tone = 'very high confidence' match to the prototype (decoded brightness >= 0.8 of the bold colour); weak_orbital (2) = subdued tone = 'high / intermediate confidence'; mixed prototypes containing it (Carb. + 2.2um) are capped at weak_orbital; not_detected (0) = the pixel was confidently classified as a DIFFERENT prototype. confirmed_in_situ (4) is set ONLY within the position uncertainty (10-50 m radius, per sample) of sample POIs 4, 5, 6, 7, where a source states the mineral was measured in situ (see each POI description); those marks are unit/section-level statements applied at a derived position, and they override the orbital tier there.
Does NOT measure: Abundance, grain size or how much of a pixel is this mineral. A prototype is the closest match to a published spectrum; the map's own readme says exact attributions can only be verified by further analysis. not_detected means a different prototype was the best match, NOT absence of the mineral: this is a dominant-mineralogy map, so minor components are not excluded. Tier boundaries are 36 m pixels resampled to 2 m (nearest), so edges are blocky and not accurate at cell level. Dust and the unmodelled classes can hide or mimic detections. The CRISM-to-CTX/HiRISE registration residual was not measured here (the authors state they coregistered to the USGS controlled CTX/HiRISE products); expect offsets of the order of tens of metres or more relative to rover points.
Quality: -1 (no_coverage) marks pixels with NO usable classification, NOT 'nothing detected': (a) black (0,0,0), which the source defines as 'not identified as any of the known prototypes' and the Zenodo description also calls the null value; the file has no nodata mask, so unclassified pixels and areas without CRISM data cannot be told apart (26.0% of the site), and (b) edge-blend colours that could not be decoded to one prototype (residual > 14 RGB units from a scaled prototype colour; 10.3%). Decoding: the map stores confidence as colour brightness, so each colour is fitted as s x (bold prototype RGB); s >= 0.8 is read as bold (the documented bold and subdued tones are 1.0 and 0.6 of the bold RGB), 0.4 <= s < 0.8 as subdued, s < 0.4 as undecodable. The 0.8 split and the 14-unit tolerance are our choices. Four CRISM scenes of different dates and observing conditions were mosaicked, so detection sensitivity varies spatially. INTERIM layer built by the query-engine team (sitebuild/science.py) from the public source cited; to be replaced by the data pipeline's official layer when available.
